run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary:
All three indices exist and were queried (3 indices, 16/13/16 docs). Each of the three questions initially returned zero, and in each case the cause was a field-name mismatch visible in the index mappings, not an absence of ERROR logs.

1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has no `level` field (mapping: @timestamp date, message text, service keyword, severity keyword). `term {level:"ERROR"}` returned 0 over the tool's default 1h window. Re-run on the correct field, `term {severity:"ERROR"}`, over the whole authorized window 2026-10-24T19:39:16Z–2026-11-23T19:39:16Z: 10. Severity breakdown in that window: ERROR 10, INFO 6, total 16.

2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 also has no `level` field; severity is numeric `severity_num` integer. `terms {level:["ERROR","FATAL"]}` returned 0. Sampled documents show 3=[INFO] healthcheck, 5=[ERROR] DB timeout, 6=[FATAL] Disk full. `terms {severity_num:[5,6]}` returned 8 over the same full window (6 docs at 5 plus 2 docs at 6), consistent with the severity_num aggregation.

3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no `@timestamp` field at all (mapping: ingest_ts keyword, level text... precisely ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message text). The bool query with range on @timestamp plus term level:ERROR returned 0 and no error (unmapped field matches nothing). Re-run with the actual time field `ingest_ts` (keyword holding values like "2026-11-23T08:01:00", so the range is lexicographic string comparison) for 2026-11-23: 7 ERROR entries today. Context checked: 11 of the 16 docs are dated 2026-11-23, 5 are dated 2026-11-22 (all ERROR), and the level aggregation over the whole index is ERROR 12, INFO 4.

All counts are within the authorized window; these are log-content query results, so no root cause or service-impact conclusion is drawn.

claims.text: All three indices exist and are green: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 with 16 documents, app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 with 13, app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 with 16.
Mapping of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword), severity (keyword) — it contains no field named `level`.
In app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 the query {"term":{"level":"ERROR"}} returned 0 (tool default window 2026-11-23T18:39:16Z–19:39:16Z).
In app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 the corrected query {"term":{"severity":"ERROR"}} over the full authorized window 2026-10-24T19:39:16Z–2026-11-23T19:39:16Z returned 10.
Severity aggregation over the full authorized window in app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: ERROR 10, INFO 6, total 16, so every document of the index has a severity value and 10 of 16 are ERROR.
Mapping of app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3: @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer), svc (keyword) — no field named `level`.
In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 the query {"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}} returned 0.

Sampled documents of app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 tie the numeric severity field to text levels: severity_num 3 with msg prefix [INFO] (healthcheck), 5 with [ERROR] (DB timeout), 6 with [FATAL] (Disk full); all from svc order-280, timestamps 2026-11-23T19:36:01Z–19:38:05Z.
severity_num aggregation in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3: key 5 (ERROR) 6 docs, key 3 (INFO) 5 docs, key 6 (FATAL) 2 docs, total 13.
In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 the corrected query {"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}} over the full authorized window returned 8 (ERROR plus FATAL).
Mapping of app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3: ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword), message (text) — it contains no @timestamp field and no date-typed field.

In app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 the bool query with range on @timestamp (2026-11-23T00:00:00Z–23:59:59Z) plus term level:ERROR returned 0 without error, and the tool noted that no matched index maps a date field so no time filter was applied.
Documents of app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 carry ingest_ts keyword values of the form "2026-11-23T08:01:00" (no timezone) together with level ERROR, e.g. messages "err today 1/2/3".
In app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 the corrected query (range on ingest_ts 2026-11-23T00:00:00–2026-11-23T23:59:59 plus term level:ERROR) returned 7.
Level aggregation over all documents of app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3: ERROR 12, INFO 4, total 16.

In app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, 11 of the 16 documents have ingest_ts inside 2026-11-23 and 5 fall outside that day; the 5 outside are dated 2026-11-22T08:01:00–08:05:00 and all have level ERROR ("err yest 1..5").

The zero results in all three questions were caused by field names that do not exist in the respective mappings (level in indices a and b, @timestamp in index c), not by an absence of ERROR documents: the same indices contain 10, 8 and 12 ERROR/ERROR+FATAL documents under their real field names.

The numeric severity encoding in index b (3=INFO, 5=ERROR, 6=FATAL) is inferred from three sampled documents' msg prefixes; other codes outside 3/5/6 were not observed, and any code not present is unknown rather than mapped.

Query index a on severity.keyword-style field `severity` and index b on `severity_num` (5,6) rather than `level`; note that the search tool applies an implicit @timestamp filter to these two indices (defaulting to the last 1 hour), so pass an explicit start_time/end_time to cover the date range you intend.
For index c, use `ingest_ts` with a lexicographic string range; ideally reindex it as a date field so date arithmetic (e.g. "today" in a specific timezone) is well defined.

gaps: ingest_ts in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 is a keyword, so the 2026-11-23 range is a lexicographic string comparison, not a date comparison; values carry no timezone, so "today" was taken as 2026-11-23 UTC (the authorized window's end date).

The implicit @timestamp filter on indices a and b defaults to a 1-hour window; the initial zero counts for those two indices were obtained in that narrower window, so the reported 10 and 8 come from explicit full-window queries while documents outside 2026-10-24T19:39:16Z–2026-11-23T19:39:16Z were not examined.
The severity_num → level mapping for index b rests on three sampled documents; documents with severity_num values other than 3, 5 and 6 were not observed and cannot be classified.
Log counts say nothing about service health or causality; no application, trace, metric or Kubernetes evidence was consulted for this request, and none is claimed.
next_steps: If you need counts restricted to a specific day or service in indices a and b, re-run with explicit start_time/end_time (and optionally a service/svc term filter).
If a date-typed timestamp is required in index c, consider adding a date field or an index template change so @timestamp is mapped.
